4383.stem:
The braking distance of a car, in metres, is directly proportional to the square of its speed in km/h, and can be represented by the equation

$$\text{braking distance} = k \times (\text{speed})^2$$

where $k$ is the constant of variation.

The braking distance for a car travelling at 50 km/h is 20 m.

parts.latex: Find the value of $k$.
What is the braking distance when the speed of the car is 90 km/h?

solutions.latex:
Substitute the given values into the formula.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Braking distance} &= k\times(\text{speed})^2 \\ 20 &= k\times 50^2 \\ k &= \dfrac{20}{50^2} \\ &= 0.008\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correctly substitutes values into the formula, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
The following formula can be used to calculate an estimate for blood alcohol content (BAC) for males.

$$BAC_{\text{male}} = \dfrac{10N - 7.5H}{6.8M}$$

$N$ is the number of standard drinks consumed

$M$ is the person's weight in kilograms

$H$ is the number of hours of drinking

Cameron weighs 75 kg. His BAC was zero when he began drinking alcohol. At 9:00 pm, after consuming 3 standard drinks, his BAC was 0.02.

Using the formula, estimate at what time Cameron began drinking alcohol, to the nearest minute.

solutions.latex:
Substitute $BAC=0.02$, $N=3$ and $M=75$ into the formula.
$$\begin{aligned}0.02 &= \dfrac{10\times 3-7.5H}{6.8\times 75}\\ 10.2 &= 30-7.5H\\ H &= \dfrac{30-10.2}{7.5}\\ &= 2.64 \text{ hours}\\ &\approx 2 \text{ h } 38 \text{ min}\end{aligned}$$
Subtract from 9:00 pm.
$$9{:}00 \text{ pm} - 2 \text{ h } 38 \text{ min} = 6{:}22 \text{ pm}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Cameron began drinking at 6:22 pm.}$$
criteria: Substitutes values into the BAC formula, or equivalent merit

meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

parts.latex: Which of the following correctly expresses $x$ as the subject of $y = \dfrac{ax - b}{2}$?

solutions.latex:
Make $x$ the subject of $y = \dfrac{ax-b}{2}$, undoing the operations in reverse order.
$$\begin{aligned} y &= \dfrac{ax-b}{2} \\ 2y &= ax - b &&(\text{multiply by } 2) \\ 2y + b &= ax &&(\text{add } b) \\ x &= \dfrac{2y+b}{a} &&(\text{divide by } a) \end{aligned}$$
This is option A.

meta.generated_note: MCQ working written for the keyed option A.

4421.stem: The formula $C = 100n + b$ is used to calculate the cost of producing laptops, where $C$ is the cost in dollars, $n$ is the number of laptops produced and $b$ is the fixed cost in dollars.

parts.latex: Find the cost when 1943 laptops are produced and the fixed cost is \$20 180.

Some laptops have some extra features added. The formula to calculate the production cost for these is

$$C = 100n + an + 20\,180,$$

where $a$ is the additional cost in dollars per laptop produced.

Find the number of laptops produced if the additional cost is \$26 per laptop and the total production cost is \$97 040.
can_use: Changing the subject of a formula

solutions.latex:
Substitute $n = 1943$ and $b = 20\,180$ into $C = 100n + b$.
$$\begin{aligned} C &= 100 \times 1943 + 20\,180 \\ &= \$214\,480 \end{aligned}$$

meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

solutions.latex:
Substitute $a = 26$ and $C = 97\,040$ into the given formula.
$$\begin{aligned} 97\,040 &= 100n + 26n + 20\,180 \\ 97\,040 &= 126n + 20\,180 \\ 76\,860 &= 126n \\ n &= 610 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ 610 \text{ laptops were produced.}$$
criteria: Makes the correct substitution, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
The distance between Bricktown and Koala Creek is 75 km. A person travels from Bricktown to Koala Creek at an average speed of 50 km/h.

How long does it take the person to complete the journey?

solutions.latex:
Using $\text{time}=\dfrac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}}$:
$$\begin{aligned} T &= \dfrac{75}{50} \\ &= 1.5 \text{ hours} \end{aligned}$$
Since $0.5$ hours is $30$ minutes, the time is $1$ hour $30$ minutes.

$$\therefore\ \text{the journey takes 1 hour 30 minutes}$$

meta.generated_note: MCQ working written from the answer key (C).

parts.latex:
When Jake stops drinking alcohol at 10:30 pm, he has a blood alcohol content (BAC) of 0.08375.

The number of hours required for a person to reach zero BAC after they stop consuming alcohol is given by the formula

$$\text{Time} = \dfrac{\text{BAC}}{0.015}.$$

At what time on the next day should Jake expect his BAC to be 0.05?

solutions.latex:
The BAC must fall from $0.08375$ to $0.05$, a drop of
$$0.08375 - 0.05 = 0.03375$$
Using the given formula, the time for this fall is
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Time} &= \dfrac{0.03375}{0.015} \\ &= 2.25 \text{ hours} \\ &= 2 \text{ hours } 15 \text{ minutes} \end{aligned}$$
Add this to 10:30 pm:
$$10{:}30 \text{ pm} + 2\text{ h } 15\text{ min} = 12{:}45 \text{ am}$$
This is option A.

parts.latex:
The formula below can be used to estimate the blood alcohol content (BAC) of a female.

$$BAC_{Female} = \dfrac{10N - 7.5H}{5.5M}$$

where $N$ is the number of standard drinks consumed

$H$ is the number of hours of drinking

$M$ is the person's weight in kilograms

Georgia weighs 68 kg and had 6 standard drinks between 6 pm and 10 pm.

Use the given formula to estimate Georgia's BAC, correct to two decimal places.

solutions.latex:
Drinking from 6 pm to 10 pm gives $H = 4$.
$$\begin{aligned} BAC &= \dfrac{10 \times 6 - 7.5 \times 4}{5.5 \times 68} \\ &\approx 0.08 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ BAC \approx 0.08$$

parts.latex: Solve the equation $5 - x = \dfrac{2x}{3}$

solutions.latex:
Multiply both sides by $3$.
$$\begin{aligned} 15 - 3x &= 2x \\ 15 &= 5x \\ x &= 3 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ x = 3$$
criteria: Multiplies both sides by $3$, or equivalent merit

meta.marker_note: Consequential follow-through (CFPA) only if the first step is multiplying by $3$.

parts.latex:
A student is thinking of a number. Let the number be $x$.

When the student subtracts 8 from this number and multiplies the result by 3, the answer is 2 more than $x$.

Which equation can be used to find $x$?

solutions.latex:
Subtracting 8 from the number gives $x-8$, and multiplying by 3 gives $3(x-8)$.

The answer is 2 more than $x$, which is $x+2$.
$$3(x-8)=x+2$$
Option A has $2x$ instead of $x+2$. Options B and D only subtract 8 from the term $3x$, not from $x$. So option C is correct.

meta.self_check: Translated the wording directly into an equation.

parts.latex: Solve $x + \dfrac{x - 1}{2} = 9$.

solutions.latex:
Multiply both sides by $2$ to clear the fraction.
$$\begin{aligned} x + \dfrac{x-1}{2} &= 9 \\ 2x + x - 1 &= 18 \\ 3x &= 19 \\ x &= \dfrac{19}{3} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ x = \dfrac{19}{3}$$
criteria: Writes fraction using a common denominator, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: If $x = -2.531$, what is the value of $x^2$ rounded to 2 decimal places?

solutions.latex:
Squaring the value:
$$x^2 = (-2.531)^2 = 6.405961$$
The third decimal place is $5$, so round up.
$$x^2 \approx 6.41$$
Hence the answer is D.

parts.latex:
Consider the formula $s = wt + \dfrac{p}{2}$.

Which of the following correctly shows $p$ as the subject of the formula?

solutions.latex:
Make $p$ the subject of $s = wt + \dfrac{p}{2}$.

Subtract $wt$ from both sides:
$$s - wt = \dfrac{p}{2}$$
Multiply both sides by 2:
$$p = 2s - 2wt$$
This is option D.

meta.self_check: Substituted p = 2s - 2wt back: wt + (s - wt) = s.

parts.latex:
A train left Richmond at 6:42 am and arrived at Central Station at 8:04 am. The distance travelled by the train from Richmond to Central was 61 km.

What was the average speed of this train, correct to the nearest km/h?

solutions.latex:
The time taken is from 6:42 am to 8:04 am.
$$8{:}04 - 6{:}42 = 1 \text{ hour } 22 \text{ minutes} = \dfrac{82}{60} \text{ hours}$$
Using $\text{speed} = \dfrac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}$:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{speed} &= 61 \div \dfrac{82}{60} \\ &= \dfrac{61 \times 60}{82} \\ &\approx 44.6 \text{ km/h} \end{aligned}$$
To the nearest km/h this is $45$ km/h, which is option B.

4344.stem:
Sarah, a 60 kg female, consumes 3 glasses of wine at a family dinner over 2.5 hours.

Note: there are 1.2 standard drinks in one glass of wine.

The blood alcohol content (BAC) for females can be estimated by

$$BAC_{\text{female}} = \dfrac{10N - 7.5H}{5.5M},$$

where $N$ = number of standard drinks

$H$ = number of hours drinking

$M$ = mass in kilograms.

parts.latex: Calculate Sarah's BAC at the end of the dinner, correct to 3 decimal places.

The time it takes a person's BAC to reach zero is given by

$$\text{Time} = \dfrac{BAC}{0.015}.$$

Calculate the time it takes for Sarah's BAC to return to zero, assuming she stopped drinking after 2.5 hours. Give your answer to the nearest minute.

solutions.latex:
Substitute $N=1.2\times 3$, $H=2.5$, $M=60$ into the given formula.
$$\begin{aligned} BAC &= \dfrac{10(1.2\times 3)-7.5\times 2.5}{5.5\times 60} \\ &= 0.0522\ldots \\ &\approx 0.052 \text{ (to 3 decimal places)} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Attempts to use the $BAC$ formula, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: Which of the following correctly expresses $y$ as the subject of the formula $3x - 4y - 1 = 0$?

solutions.latex:
Make $y$ the subject by moving the $y$ term to one side.

$$\begin{aligned} 3x - 4y - 1 &= 0 \\ 3x - 1 &= 4y &&(\text{add } 4y) \\ y &= \dfrac{3x-1}{4} &&(\text{divide by } 4) \end{aligned}$$

Hence the answer is option C.

Time to reach zero $BAC$:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Time} &= \dfrac{0.088257\ldots}{0.015} \\ &= 5\text{ h }53\text{ min (to nearest minute)} \end{aligned}$$
Adding to 12:30 am,
$$12\text{:}30\text{ am}+5\text{ h }53\text{ min}=6\text{:}23\text{ am}$$
$$\therefore\ BAC \text{ reaches zero at } 6\text{:}23\text{ am}$$

parts.latex:
The blood alcohol content ($BAC$) for males can be estimated by

$$BAC_{\text{male}} = \dfrac{10N - 7.5H}{6.8M}$$

where

$N$ = number of standard drinks

$H$ = number of hours drinking

$M$ = the person’s weight in kilograms.

The number of hours for a person’s $BAC$ to reach zero is given by

$$\text{Time} = \dfrac{BAC}{0.015}.$$

Henry, a 72 kg male, consumes a total of three drinks at a family dinner.

The drinks are:

\begin{itemize}
\item two 375 mL cans of beer that hold 1.4 standard drinks each
\item one 250 mL can of mixer that holds 1.8 standard drinks.
\end{itemize}

It took 2 hours and 10 minutes for Henry’s $BAC$ to return to zero.

How many hours did Henry take to consume the three drinks, correct to the nearest hour?

solutions.latex:
The time for the $BAC$ to reach zero is 2 hours 10 minutes, so
$$\begin{aligned} 2\dfrac{10}{60} &= \dfrac{BAC}{0.015} \\ BAC &= 2\dfrac{10}{60} \times 0.015 \\ &= 0.0325 \end{aligned}$$
Number of drinks:
$$N = 2 \times 1.4 + 1.8 = 4.6$$
Substituting into the $BAC$ formula with $M = 72$:
$$\begin{aligned} 0.0325 &= \dfrac{(10 \times 4.6) - 7.5H}{6.8 \times 72} \\ 15.912 &= 46 - 7.5H \\ -30.088 &= -7.5H \\ H &= \dfrac{-30.088}{-7.5} = 4.0117\ldots \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ H \approx 4 \text{ hours}$$
criteria: Uses the $BAC$ formula, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Consider the formula $n = \dfrac{m-p}{q}$.

Which of the following correctly shows $p$ as the subject of the formula?

solutions.latex:
Start with the formula and make $p$ the subject.
$$\begin{aligned} n &= \dfrac{m-p}{q}\\ nq &= m - p &&(\text{multiply by } q)\\ p &= m - nq &&(\text{rearrange}) \end{aligned}$$
So the answer is option B.
